topic_tag: a shared school and a rivalry between towns
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.

worlds.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. Its classes mixed students from both towns, as did its only sports team, and by the 1940s most families had in-laws across the bridge. In 1951 the two councils split the cost of repairing the bridge at a single meeting, and a survey that year found fewer than one in ten residents who could say which town had refused to pay. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
worlds.explanation: Mixed classes and intermarriage led to a quick shared bridge repair and a quarrel almost no one remembered, so the school "defused" the rivalry. "Formalized" fails because the school mixed the towns rather than organizing them against each other. "Embellished" fails because the quarrel was being forgotten, and "commercialized" fails because with only one mixed team there was no rivalry event to sell.

formalized.quote: Its classes mixed students from both towns
formalized.why: Mixing the towns gave the rivalry no organized structure.

embellished.quote: fewer than one in ten residents who could say
embellished.why: A nearly forgotten quarrel was not being retold with additions.

commercialized.why: With one mixed team there was no contest between the towns to profit from.

worlds.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. It assigned each student to a house named for his home town, with a handbook setting out how points were won in contests each term, and who kept the trophy; only students and teachers watched. The handbook's account of the bridge quarrel matches the 1870 court papers line for line, and police records show fights between the towns' residents rising after each contest. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
worlds.explanation: Houses by town, written point rules, scheduled contests, and a trophy gave the rivalry an official structure, so the school "formalized" it. "Defused" fails because fights rose after each contest. "Embellished" fails because the handbook matched the court papers, and "commercialized" fails because the contests had no outside audience to pay.

defused.quote: fights between the towns' residents rising

embellished.quote: matches the 1870 court papers line for line

commercialized.why: With no outside audience, nothing was sold.

worlds.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. Its history teachers retold the bridge quarrel every year with a drowned mayor and a stolen church bell, neither found in the 1870 court papers or any newspaper of the time. Its teams always mixed students from both towns and its events were free, and surveys in the 1930s found graduates more hostile to the other town than their parents were. A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
worlds.explanation: Teachers retold the quarrel each year with events found in no record, so the school "embellished" the rivalry. "Defused" fails because graduates were more hostile than their parents. "Formalized" fails because the teams mixed the towns, and "commercialized" fails because its events were free.

defused.quote: more hostile to the other town than their parents

formalized.quote: always mixed students from both towns
formalized.why: The school gave the rivalry no organized form.

worlds.passage: Two towns in a narrow valley had quarreled since 1870 over who should pay for the bridge between them. In 1924 they opened a single high school for both. Short of money, its board sold two shopkeepers the right to print each town's color on pennants and mugs, and the 1930 budget lists those royalties as the school's largest income after taxes. The goods bore nothing but a town's color, sold best among students from both towns around the bridge's anniversary, and were advertised with the line "show the other side." A local historian later wrote that the new school had ______ the rivalry between the two towns.
worlds.explanation: The board turned the towns' colors into licensed goods that earned the school royalties and sold on the rivalry, so it "commercialized" the rivalry. "Defused" fails because advertisements kept urging each side against the other. "Formalized" fails because the board only licensed merchandise and set up no contests or rules, and "embellished" fails because the goods told no story at all.

defused.why: Merchandise selling on hostility kept the rivalry alive.

formalized.quote: sold two shopkeepers the right to print
formalized.why: The school's role was licensing goods, not giving the rivalry rules or events.

embellished.quote: bore nothing but a town's color
embellished.why: Goods with no story added nothing to the tale of the quarrel.
